rulers.title: King of Italy

ledger.note: 19 September 855: the Treaty of Prum gives Louis II Italy. 'Treaty of Prum, 19 September 855' (infobox: partition from Middle Francia); Louis II 'inherited the imperial crown, and rule over the Carolingian Italy'. The Louis II page: 'On the death of his father in September 855, he became sole emperor'. Written as a hand-over: Louis II had been king of Italy since 844.
863: Louis II receives Provence. 'In 863, upon the death of his brother Charles, Louis received the kingdom of Provence.' The page does not name Arles, Aix or Embrun.

875: Provence leaves the Italian crown. Louis II 'died, near Ghedi ... on 12 August 875'; the page is silent on who took Provence and on his successors' years ('Charles the Bald' is only named in the infobox, 'Carloman' in the text). Bridged at confidence 1 from the Lower Burgundy row that Cliopatria draws on Provence.
887: the royal seat moves to Verona. 'As king, Berengar made his seat at Verona, which he heavily fortified.' (Pavia is named only as the place of his first charter.)

November 887: Charles the Fat is deposed and Berengar of Friuli takes Italy. Berengar was 'elected to replace Charles in Italy after his deposition in November 887'; charters begin his reign at Pavia between 26 December 887 and 2 January 888 (disputed). The Kingdom page gives the deposition as 887 and 888.

889: Guy of Spoleto wins the crown. 'Early in 889, their truce having expired, Guy defeated Berengar at the Battle of the Trebbia' and 'made himself sole king in Italy'; Berengar 'remained master in Friuli' at Verona. The infobox has Guy disputing the throne 888-894.

region.text: the Po plain from Pavia to the Trebbia and Bergamo

ledger.note: 889: the Trebbia. Guy of Spoleto beats Berengar and holds the kingdom; the two fight over the Po plain until Lambert's death in 898 ('In 894, Arnulf and Berengar defeated Guy at Bergamo').

894-896: the Carolingians briefly hold Italy. 'Carolingians once briefly regained the throne in 894-896' (Kingdom page); the Berengar page has Arnulf and Berengar beating Guy at Bergamo in 894. Berengar kept Italy as Arnulf's vassal from 888 (Trent).

region.text: the whole kingdom, as Cliopatria draws it in 896-897

ledger.note: 896: Arnulf's army in Italy. 'Berengar was with Arnulf's army that invaded Italy in 896' (Berengar page) and the Carolingians 'briefly regained the throne in 894-896' (Kingdom page); Cliopatria draws the whole of Italy as East Franks in 896-897, and Berengar 'was removed from Friuli and replaced with Waltfred' after 896.

region.text: the eastern half between the Adda and the Po

ledger.note: 898: the north-east is Berengar's again. Lambert's pact gave Berengar 'the eastern half between the Adda and the Po' (year not stated); Cliopatria returns this half in 898.

region.text: the rest of the kingdom: western Lombardy, Piedmont, Liguria, Emilia, Tuscany and the Spoleto lands

ledger.note: October 898: Berengar becomes sole king. 'Lambert died within days, on 15 October 898. Days later Berengar had secured Pavia and become sole ruler.' Cliopatria draws the whole kingdom from 899.

region.text: the Po plain from Pavia to the Trebbia and Bergamo

ledger.note: October 898: the war with Spoleto ends with Lambert's death.

region.text: the Lombard kingdom around Pavia and Verona

ledger.note: 900: Louis the Blind invades Italy. 'In 900, Louis marched into Italy and defeated Berengar'; Cliopatria draws the whole of Italy as his Kingdom of Lower Burgundy until 910.

region.text: the Lombard kingdom around Pavia and Verona

ledger.note: 21 July 905: Louis is captured at Verona and blinded. 'Berengar defeated him at Verona, captured him, and ordered him to be blinded on 21 July' (905).

29 July 923: Rudolf II beats Berengar at Fiorenzuola. 'On 29 July 923, the forces of Rudolph, Adalbert and Berengar of Ivrea met those of Berengar' and 'defeated him in the Battle of Fiorenzuola'; Rudolf had been invited in 921. Cliopatria draws the whole of Italy as 'Upper Burgundy and Italy' in 922-925.
7 April 924: Berengar I is murdered at Verona. 'Murdered at Verona by one of his own men', 'possibly at Rudolph's instigation'; infobox '7 April 924'.

925: the capital returns to Pavia. Berengar's seat was Verona; the Kingdom page names Pavia as the capital 'at least to 1024'. After his death 'Berengar's partisans now elected Hugh as king (925)' (Hugh page).
926: Rudolf II is driven out. 'Rudolph was ejected from Italy in 926 and Hugh crossed the Alps to be crowned.'
926: Hugh of Arles is crowned king of Italy. 'Rather than accept Rudolph, Berengar's partisans now elected Hugh as king (925)'; crowned after he 'crossed the Alps' in 926; infobox 'Reign: 926-947'.

928: Hugh annexes Provence to Italy de facto. 'Louis died on 5 June 928 and Hugh returned to Provence to sort out a succession'; 'Hugh annexed the kingdom to Italy de facto, issuing diplomata concerning Provence from his Italian chancery in a royal style' (Hugh page). He had been regent in Lower Burgundy and Provence since 911; Cliopatria draws Italy and Provence as one 'Kingdom of Lower Burgundy' for 926-935. [Reviewer eu-13-b, 2026-10-25: year moved from 926 to 928 and confidence raised from 1 to 2 on the Hugh page.]
933: Provence handed to Rudolf. 'He concluded a treaty with Rudolph in 933 by which Rudolf abandoned his claims to Italy in return for being handed Provence.'

951: Otto I invades. 'In 951 he invaded the kingdom and proclaimed himself king.' Berengar II is Berengar of Ivrea, the page's 'Otto's rival', who returned from exile in 945 and by 947 held 'much of the real power' (Hugh page).

region.text: the March of Verona: Friuli with Verona

ledger.note: 952: the March of Verona goes to Bavaria. 'The March of Verona was annexed by Bavaria in 952 and remained part of the Kingdom of Germany.' The page gives no boundary; Friuli with Verona is the researcher's reading.
952: the invasion settles. The Kingdom page is silent on the settlement; the Kingdom of Germany dossier dates the oath of fealty and the cession of Friuli to August 952. Bridged at confidence 1.
961: Otto I conquers Pavia and is proclaimed king of Italy. 'Conquered Pavia in 961', 'Otto was proclaimed king of Italy at Pavia'; he was crowned emperor at Rome on 2 February 962 (infobox).

961: the Italian kingdom passes to the German king. The kingdom continues inside the Empire from 962 as a non-sovereign elective monarchy (infobox), drawn by Cliopatria's Holy Roman Empire shape; Cliopatria's own row runs to 969.

wars.name: Louis II's capture of Bari
wars.outcome: Bari 'succumbed in 871' with Louis II's help; he was 'robbed and imprisoned by Adelchis, prince of Benevento, in August 871'. No land changed hands on the page.
wars.note: The page also says he marched into the south in the year of his imperial coronation (850).

wars.name: Berengar I against Guy and Lambert of Spoleto

zones.text: the Po plain from Pavia to the Trebbia and Bergamo

wars.outcome: Guy won at the Trebbia in early 889 and held the crown; Arnulf and Berengar beat him at Bergamo in 894; Lambert's death on 15 October 898 left Berengar sole ruler.

wars.name: Arnulf of Carinthia's Italian campaigns
wars.outcome: The Carolingians 'briefly regained the throne in 894-896' (Kingdom page); Berengar, Arnulf's vassal since 888, was with Arnulf's army in 896. No contest is recorded because the pages show Berengar on Arnulf's side.

wars.name: Hungarian invasion of Italy (899)
wars.outcome: 'They invaded Italy first in 899'; Berengar's army 'was surprised and routed near the Brenta River' on 24 September 899. No change of border on the page.

wars.name: Louis the Blind's invasions of Italy

zones.text: the Lombard kingdom around Pavia and Verona

wars.outcome: Louis defeated Berengar in 900; Berengar defeated him at Verona, captured and blinded him on 21 July 905.
wars.note: The Lower Burgundy dossier splits this into 900-902 and 905; the Berengar page gives only 900 and 905.

wars.name: Rudolf II's war for Italy
wars.outcome: Rudolf II, invited in 921, beat Berengar at Fiorenzuola on 29 July 923; Berengar was murdered on 7 April 924; Hugh was elected in 925 and Rudolf was ejected in 926.

wars.name: Berengar of Ivrea against Hugh
wars.outcome: Hugh expelled Berengar of Ivrea in 941; Berengar returned from Germany in 945 and defeated Hugh; by 947 'much of the real power' was in Berengar's hands. Hugh retired to Provence and died on 10 April 948.
wars.note: An internal succession struggle, not a territorial war.

wars.name: Otto I's invasions of Italy
wars.outcome: Otto invaded in 951 and proclaimed himself king; the March of Verona went to Bavaria in 952; he conquered Pavia in 961 and was crowned emperor in 962.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Prum of 855 divided the Middle Kingdom among Lothair I's sons, but the pages give the Italian frontier only by regions and cities, never by line; the March of Verona (952) is the one boundary named.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by the Phase B agent for batch eu-13-b. Medieval half of the split of Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Italy' row (587..1946): shapes 887-969 are reviewed here (the Lombard shapes 587-774 are in kingdom-of-the-lombards, the shapes of 1862-1946 in kingdom-of-italy). The dossier starts in 855, not 887: the neighbouring dossiers (middle-franks, lower-burgundy) already name this state as the successor of Middle Francia and the holder of Provence in 863, and Cliopatria draws Italy in 850-859 as Middle Franks and in 860-886 as West Franks (a gap-filler should check that the west-franks and middle-franks dossiers remove Italy from those shapes). The keyframes 855, 900, 922 and 952 are new.
Pages: four of the five allowed for 8 shapes (Kingdom of Italy (Holy Roman Empire), Berengar I, Hugh of Italy, Louis II of Italy); the fourth is an extra over the budget of the Kingdom of Italy row as a whole, justified by the 855-886 gap. The Kingdom page gives no area, no reign years for 774-962 and no territorial detail, so most events rest on the person pages.
Not settled: (1) Rome and the Papal States: the page does not place them inside the kingdom; Cliopatria's Papal States row stays separate throughout and no event is recorded. (2) Spoleto and Camerino: the page is silent on their status 888-961; they are in the 888 shape (Guy's lands) and the shape stays drawn whole. (3) Louis II's successors 875-887 (Charles the Bald, Carloman, Charles the Fat) have no years on the pages; no event or ruler entry for them; Charles the Fat's deposition is 887 (lead) or 888 (body) on the Kingdom page, November 887 on the Berengar page. (4) The 894-896 Carolingian interlude: the pages show Berengar on Arnulf's side (vassal from 888) and Cliopatria draws East Franks for 896-897; the east-franks dossier holds the contest. (5) Berengar's imperial coronation (December 915), Lothair II's coronation (April 931) and Berengar II's accession (950) have no territorial effect and are in the ruler strip only. (6) The 902 break in Louis the Blind's invasion (Lower Burgundy dossier) is not on the Berengar page. (7) The northern and Frankish side of 952-961 (Berengar II as Otto's vassal) is the Kingdom of Germany dossier's; none of it is on the pages opened here. (8) Friuli (a march) and Istria are not Cliopatria rows; the March of Verona is not either.
Slug change for neighbours: dossiers that name this state as 'kingdom-of-italy' for 855-961 (middle-franks, lower-burgundy, upper-burgundy, east-franks, kingdom-of-germany, holy-roman-empire, march-of-verona) should now read kingdom-of-italy-medieval; 'kingdom-of-italy' is the 1861-1946 state.
Place names the gazetteer may lack: Pavia and Verona as places (provinces are used where a region is needed); 'Friuli' and 'Provence' are regions.
Page budget: see the sibling dossiers; this state used four pages.
